## 01
The request
Like ordering at a counter: the app writes a short note and hands it over

Your phone never talks to the AI directly

Your appthe customer
The APIthe counter
The modelthe kitchen
1 · The order POST /v1/answers
2 · Checks the key, passes it on
3 · The answer, word by word
4 · Shown on your screen

The order is a note with three parts

cURLPythonJavaScript
answer = client.answers.create( model="small-fast", messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Summarise this email"}], max_tokens=200, ) # answer.text holds the reply
modelWhich cook. Small ones are faster and cheaper
messagesWhat you want, in normal words
max_tokensHow long the answer may be, at most

## 02
The answer
It comes back in small pieces, and each piece has a price

You pay per piece of text, not per question

Can you summarise this email for me?
0
pieces (tokens) in this short question
≈ 400
for a 300-word email, about one page
¾
of an English word per token, on average
Approximate · each model splits text in its own way

Three replies cover almost every case

200
OK
Here is your answer.
The dish arrives at the table
429
Too many requests
Slow down and try again in a moment.
The kitchen asks you to wait
500
Server error
Something broke on their side.
The oven stopped; not your fault
Correction
The video says the AI "remembers your earlier chats". It does not: the app sends the whole conversation again with every request.
It remembers → The app resends it

## 03
Start small
One key, one request, one answer: enough to see how it works

Three steps to your first answer

1
Get a key
It works like a house key: whoever has it can spend on your account
2
Send one request
Pick a model, write your question, set max_tokens
3
Read the reply
Check the status first: 200 means the text is there
Tip
Set a monthly spending limit before you share the app with anyone.
